subject: RE: Demo streaming cut-off — quick mitigation & patch plan
messages:
From: Sam Rodgers <sam@acmeops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Urgent: Streaming cut off in demo (AcmeOps PoC)

Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough. During the final demo our transcript stream abruptly stopped and the assistant returned a partial, repeated token sequence (we saw about ~6 repeated word fragments). I'm attaching the console logs and the screen recording; the behavior happened twice in the same conversation. This is blocking our exec team — they want to see a reliable streaming demo to sign off on the pilot.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west (we selected it in the dashboard)
- Model: redwood-open-variant-3b (default streaming)
- Steps that reproduced it: type long prompt with ~1,800 tokens + user context (attached recording)

Can you escalate? We can demo again today if there's a fix or workaround.

Sam
Director, Platform — AcmeOps

Attachments: acme_demo_logs.txt (7KB), acme_demo_recording.mp4 (20MB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Team — forwarding urgent report from AcmeOps. TL;DR: streaming aborted mid-response in us-west during PoC; customer is at an exec sign-off.

Immediate asks: 
- Can runtime triage whether this is kv-cache eviction/GPU memory GC or a networking hiccup?
- If a quick server-side mitigation exists (route to fallback variant or increase streaming timeout), please advise so I can relay to Sam within the hour.
- If we need an SDK hotfix (reconnect/idempotency token), what's the minimum safe workaround for today?

I attached their logs and a short hotpatch plan I sketched (hotpatch_plan.md). If we can flip a config or route them to non-streaming fallback for the demo, that would be ideal.

Ben Carter

Date: 2026-09-02T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Urgent: Streaming cut off in demo (AcmeOps PoC)

Ben — thanks for the flag and the artifacts. I pulled the logs; initial signal: two streaming sessions in the same customer conversation hit a sudden ~15% spike in sequence-length memory due to long system+user.prompt (the pipeline attempted a prefix KV cache compaction and triggered a quick GC in the serving node). That GC aligns with the timestamps in the logs.

Short-term mitigation I can roll in minutes (non-invasive):
- Route the customer's requests to the stable variant (redwood-open-variant-3b-stable) in us-west that has GC thresholds relaxed for long-context demos. This is a routing flip, no model reload.
- Temporarily increase the streaming socket keepalive and 3s reconnect grace on the edge LB for their sessions.

Longer-term: we should add an observability metric to detect KV-cache compaction in real time and a runtime flag we can flip per-customer. Also we need an SDK handshake improvement to surface mid-stream truncation and attempt an automatic reconnect with idempotency token.

Can Karthik estimate risk/time for a config flip and an SDK quick patch? If we can route and increase keepalive now I can tell Sam to retry the live demo in ~15 mins.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T11:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: Urgent: Streaming cut off in demo (AcmeOps PoC) — mitigation steps

Thanks for the quick triage notes, Marissa. Confirming the logs show a KV-cache compaction event kicked off at the same ms the socket broke (see log mark GC#1872). Repro is plausible when total context > ~1,500 tokens + repeated system messages.

Immediate mitigation (low-risk, I can patch infra now):
1) Flip routing for AcmeOps to redwood-open-variant-3b-stable in us-west: runtime routing rule INF-4521. Canary to 10% for 10m -> 50% 15m -> 100% if clean.
2) Edge keepalive: set streaming.keepalive_ms=60000 (from 15000) and reconnect.grace_ms=3000. This makes transient GC pauses less likely to be perceived as socket failures.

SDK mitigation (quick dev):
- I'll create a small SDK change that sets an idempotency header X-RW-ID when starting a streaming session and on reconnect attempts we will send the last token offset to resume. Implementation ETA: 2 engineer-days for a minimal version (v0.9.7-hotfix). Risk: low, needs a patch release and ops verification.

Commands I'll run (ops):
- apply-routing --acct=AcmeOps --rule=INF-4521 --target=redwood-open-variant-3b-stable --canary=10 --window=600
- update-edge-config --key=streaming.keepalive_ms --value=60000 --scope=us-west --dry-run=false

I'll create JIRA INF-4521 and link to this thread. Can someone from SE confirm we should proceed with the canary? If yes, I'll run the flip and monitor for 45m.

-Karthik
Senior Runtime Engineer
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Urgent: Streaming cut off in demo (AcmeOps PoC) — temporary mitigation in place

Sam — quick update and apologies for the disruption during the demo. We diagnosed a transient KV-cache compaction in the us-west serving node that can cause a brief pause in streaming under very long contexts. We've applied a targeted mitigation for your PoC session:

What we did (now live):
- Routed your account to redwood-open-variant-3b-stable in us-west (canary rollout started).
- Increased streaming keepalive to 60s and added a 3s reconnect grace window at the edge.

What to expect:
- You should be able to run the same demo flow without the abrupt cut-offs. If you still see pauses, please try the non-streaming fallback option in the dashboard (Generate -> Non-streaming) — that will guarantee a single complete response.

Next steps:
- Karthik will open INF-4521 for the SDK hotfix (idempotent reconnect) and we aim to ship v0.9.7-hotfix in the next 3 business days.
- We'll set up a short follow-up demo at 15:30 PT today to verify. Are you available?

Thanks for the patience — we know this is a high-visibility moment for your team and we'll treat it as a high-priority POC issue until sign-off.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
